newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in evening.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in evening.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Friday in thin trade with most traders sidelined before tonight's issue of the U.S. payroll employment figures, dealers said.
"The market has been quiet since morning with most traders not doing anything till the release of tonight's payroll employment figures," a local dealer said.

The May U.S. payroll employment figure was expected to reach around 219,000 compared with 142,000 in the previous report. The unemployment rate was seen reaching 5.0 percent compared with the previous 4.9 percent.
The April wholesale investment index showed an increase of about 0.7 percent while consumer credit reached a hefty US$4.3 billion compared with $2.0 billion in the previous report.
The May CIBCR and ECRI inflation indicators reached 104.3 and 109.3 points, respectively.

Day-to-day, weekend and week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent. Among term rates, one month remained at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months was unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent, six-months was steady at 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent and twelve-months unchanged at 6-3/16 6-1/16 percent. - Singapore newsroom (65-870-3085)
